title: Collision energy revisited
target: Use energy as well as momentum to classify a collision.
criteria: Calculate total momentum before and after.
Account for reduced kinetic energy without losing total energy.

authoring.limitations: Reasoning evidence only. Multiple choice does not certify physical performance. Teacher reviews before assigning and rates mastery separately.

cpa.prompt: A 2 kg cart moves at +3 m/s and a 1 kg cart at −2 m/s. What is their total momentum?
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Apply the physical relationship to new data.

cpa.prompt: Two carts stick together during a collision with negligible external impulse. Which quantity must be conserved for both carts together?
options: Kinetic energy in every sticking collision.
cpa.guide: Negligible external impulse conserves system momentum.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

cpa.prompt: A 2 kg cart at +3 m/s sticks to a stationary 1 kg cart. What is their shared final speed?
cpa.guide: Initial momentum 6; total mass 3; final speed 6/3 = 2 m/s.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Apply the physical relationship to new data.

cpa.prompt: For a 2 kg cart at 3 m/s sticking to a stationary 1 kg cart, final speed is 2 m/s. What happens to total kinetic energy?
options: It falls from 18 J to 12 J.
It falls from 9 J to 6 J.
It increases from 6 J to 9 J.
cpa.guide: Initial K = ½(2)(9) = 9 J; final K = ½(3)(4) = 6 J.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Apply the physical relationship to new data.

cpa.prompt: A collision reduces the system’s kinetic energy by 7 J. What is a consistent destination?
options: Automatic loss of all system momentum.
cpa.guide: Kinetic energy can transform while total energy remains conserved.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

cpa.prompt: A report says momentum was conserved, so kinetic energy must also have been conserved. What is the flaw?
options: Any conserved momentum implies zero velocity.
Momentum and kinetic energy are the same quantity.
Momentum conservation alone does not establish an elastic collision.
Kinetic energy is never conserved in any collision.
cpa.guide: Check kinetic energy separately; inelastic collisions can conserve momentum.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Select a claim supported by the stated evidence and assumptions.
